## Purpose

This report independently reproduces the data-preparation assignment and compares the result produced by the coding agent with `data/processed/final_data.csv`. The original preparation script and final dataset are not overwritten.

## Create the comparison dataset

```{r}
# Run this report from the project root.
source("scripts/create_compared_final_data.R")
```

The four mortality files are reshaped with one reusable function. Disaster records are restricted to earthquakes and droughts in 2000--2019. Conflict deaths are summed within country-year, classified using the 25-death threshold, and lagged by moving the exposure forward one year. All sources are then joined by `iso` and `year`.

## Validate the output

```{r}
stopifnot(
  nrow(compared_final_data) == 186 * 20,
  !anyDuplicated(compared_final_data[c("iso", "year")]),
  all(range(compared_final_data$year) == c(2000, 2019)),
  all(compared_final_data$earthquake %in% 0:1),
  all(compared_final_data$drought %in% 0:1),
  all(compared_final_data$armed_conflict %in% 0:1)
)

data.frame(
  rows = nrow(compared_final_data),
  countries = n_distinct(compared_final_data$iso),
  first_year = min(compared_final_data$year),
  last_year = max(compared_final_data$year),
  duplicate_country_years = sum(duplicated(compared_final_data[c("iso", "year")]))
)
```

## Compare with the original result

```{r}
original_final_data <- read_csv(
  "data/processed/final_data.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  na = c("", "NA")
) |>
  arrange(iso, year)

comparison_summary <- tibble(
  variable = names(compared_final_data),
  differing_rows = map_int(
    names(compared_final_data),
    ~ {
      original_value <- original_final_data[[.x]]
      compared_value <- compared_final_data[[.x]]
      both_present <- !is.na(original_value) & !is.na(compared_value)
      same_present <- if (is.numeric(original_value)) {
        near(original_value, compared_value)
      } else {
        original_value == compared_value
      }
      same_value <- (is.na(original_value) & is.na(compared_value)) |
        (both_present & same_present)
      sum(!same_value)
    }
  )
)

comparison_summary
```

## Conclusion

The row keys and substantive source values agree. The differences are in `earthquake` and `drought`: the original pipeline leaves unmatched country-years as missing after its joins, whereas a binary indicator must equal zero when no qualifying event is recorded. The coding-agent version therefore replaces missing joined indicators with zero. The conflict indicator already agrees in every row, and the new pipeline explicitly applies the same zero-fill rule for safety. It is also more concise because it applies one mortality function to a named file vector and reduces the resulting tables into one dataset.

The independently generated CSV is saved as `data/processed/compared_final_data.csv`.
